text:
John Carlson's first season in Tampa has started with a burst you don't usually see from a 36-year-old defenseman. He has 5 goals and 10 points in 16 games, including goals in back-to-back games at the end of October, and he is shooting 13.2 percent, about double the league norm for defensemen. That part will settle down: he has 2.86 expected goals, so roughly two of the five are hot finishing.

The rest looks sturdy. Tampa takes 58.2 percent of the expected goals with him on the ice at 5v5, and he is better than the team without him. Evolving-Hockey had him at 2.5 wins last season, 17th among defensemen, built mostly on even-strength offense. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking still has him in the 93rd percentile for setting up shots. The weakness it flags is the old one: only 31 percent of his exits keep possession, so watch for clears off the glass when he's forechecked hard.

A Stanley Cup winner with Washington in 2018, he is a smart fit for a team that wants someone to move the puck.
headline: Carlson, at 36, is scoring like it's 2018
